reason: The plan draws only the fort walls (exposed stretches and a dashed reconstruction of the outer and inner faces), the excavation trenches, one small structure and the site grid. None of the walls, trenches or the structure can be seen in the 2010, 2014, 2022 or 2026 imagery. The mound itself is visible: tree-covered north and east slopes meet in a rounded apex that corresponds to the fort's north-east corner, but its west and south sides merge with scrub, a burial ground and field boundaries, so no second or third corner can be identified with confidence. One class C point is not enough for a registration.

candidates_considered.feature: north-east outer corner of the fort wall (drawn as exposed, plan px about (424, 27))
candidates_considered.why: the wall itself is under trees; the mound's tree-covered north and east slopes meet in a rounded apex near mosaic (548, 350) of kanmer_z18_w8432 (2014 image) whose inner edge matches the drawn corner, but this single class C point cannot be registered alone

candidates_considered.feature: north-west outer corner of the fort wall (drawn as exposed, plan px about (3, 280))
candidates_considered.why: the tree band of the north slope ends where it meets a straight field boundary running north-south; the field boundary, not the drawn wall, may set that end, so the corner cannot be identified

candidates_considered.feature: exposed stretches of the north and east arms (outer face and later veneer) and of the inner face
candidates_considered.why: no wall lines visible: the slopes over them are tree-covered in every release, and the stretches are 1 to 2 m wide lines that would need open trenches to show

candidates_considered.feature: south-east and south-west corners and the west and south arms (dashed reconstruction with short exposed stretches in trenches)
candidates_considered.why: conjectural on the plan; on the ground the mound's south and west sides have no distinct edge (open scrub, graves on the west and south-west slopes, a pond-like hollow to the south-east)

candidates_considered.feature: trenches (5 m grid squares, the large stepped cuttings at the north-east corner and in the centre, and the small trenches over the arms)
candidates_considered.why: not visible as cuts, spoil or patches in the 2010-11-20 image (release 10, available only at zoom 17, 1.1 m per pixel) or in the 2014, 2022 and 2026 images; presumably backfilled or overgrown after the 2005-2009 seasons

candidates_considered.feature: structure drawn in red in trench Z30
candidates_considered.why: a few metres across, inside the backfilled central area; not visible
no permanent marks on the ground; the paper names no datum

candidates_considered.feature: modern Hanuman shrine on the western wall and the graves on the west and south-west slopes (named in the text, not drawn on the plan)
candidates_considered.why: not on the plan; a small building on the west side of the mound in the 2022 and 2026 images may be the shrine, but it cannot be placed on the plan

notes: The site was located from the paper's Fig. 2 (a perspective digital elevation model with a UTM zone 42 grid, E 690300-690500, N 2590900-2591150), which places it about 150 m from the published coordinates, west of the north-south highway and north of Kanmer village. The squarish mound with tree-covered north and east slopes lies inside that box. Viewing the plan reduced to the imagery scale beside the 2026 image shows the drawn north and east arms (about 110 m and 120 m) roughly matching the inner edges of the tree bands (about 100 m and 110 m), which supports the identification of the site and of the north-east corner but gives only that one point. Imagery dates per release were read from each Wayback release's metadata service. Orientation statements met while reading the paper for context: on printed p. 361 (PDF page index 6) the text says the fortification is not on the cardinal directions and gives a compass direction for it; on printed p. 364 (PDF page index 9) it gives a direction for the furnace and says the house plans follow the orientation of the fort. These were read before their content was recognised; they played no part in the search, which found no usable point.
